bracket: [Textbook answer-key error in part (i), an inequality printed the wrong way round. The question asks for the compounds in order of DECREASING \(pK_b\), and the key lists them in the same sequence as the answer below but joins them with \(<\), which asserts that aniline has the SMALLEST \(pK_b\) — i.e. that it is the strongest base of the four, the reverse of the truth. The book's own Table 9.3 settles it: aniline \(9.38\), N-methylaniline \(9.30\), ethylamine \(3.29\), diethylamine \(3.00\), which is exactly the decreasing order given below. That this is a slip rather than a house convention is shown by the same key entry using \(>\) correctly in part (iv) and \(<\) correctly in parts (v) and (vi). The sequence of compounds is right in both; only the symbol is wrong. Parts (ii) to (vi) agree term for term.]
